source_text: Ιʹ. Περὶ μὲν γὰρ τοῦ Πατρὸς, τί χρὴ καὶ λέγειν, οὗ καὶ τὸ παρὰ πάντων συγκεχωρηκὸς φείδεσθαι ταῖς φυσικαῖς ἐννοίαις προκατειλημμένων; Εἰ καὶ τῆς ἀτιμίας τὰ πρῶτα ἠνέγκατο, πρῶτος τμηθεὶς εἰς Ἀγαθὸν καὶ Δημιουργὸν παρὰ τῆς ἀρχαίας καινοτομίας. Περὶ δὲ τοῦ Υἱοῦ, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, σκοπεῖτε ὡς ἁπλῶς καὶ συντόμως διαλεξώμεθα. Εἰ μέν τις ἔχοι τούτων τι λέγειν τρεπτὸν ἢ ἀλλοιωτὸν, ἢ χρόνῳ, ἢ τόπῳ, ἢ δυνάμει, ἢ ἐνεργείᾳ μετρούμενον, ἢ οὐ φυσικῶς ἀγαθὸν, ἢ οὐκ αὐτοκίνητον, ἢ οὐκ αὐτεξούσιον, ἢ λειτουργὸν, ἢ ὑμνῳδὸν, ἢ φοβού μενον, ἢ ἐλευθερούμενον, ἢ οὐ συναριθμούμενον· δεικνύτω τοῦτο, καὶ ἡμεῖς στέρξομεν, συνδούλων σεμνότητι δοξαζόμενοι, εἰ καὶ Θεὸν ζημιούμεθα. Εἰ δὲ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει ὁ Πατὴρ, τοῦ Υἱοῦ ἐστι, πλὴν τῆς αἰτίας· πάντα δὲ ὅσα τοῦ Υἱοῦ, καὶ τοῦ Πνεύ ματος, πλὴν τῆς υἱότητος, καὶ τῶν ὅσα σωματικῶς περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγεται διὰ τὸν ἐμὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ τὴν ἐμὴν σωτηρίαν, ἵνα τὸ ἐμὸν λαβὼν, τὸ ἑαυτοῦ χαρίσηται διὰ τῆς καινῆς ἀνακράσεως· παύσασθε παραληροῦντες ὀψὲ γοῦν, ὦ σοφισταὶ κενῶν ῥη μάτων, αὐτοῦ πιπτόντων. Καὶ ἵνα τί ἀποθνήσκετε, οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ, ἵν' ἐκ τῆς Γραφῆς ὑμᾶς ὀδύρωμαι; ΙΑʹ. Ὡς ἔγωγε αἰδοῦμαι μὲν τὰς τοῦ Λόγου προσηγορίας, τοσαύτας τε οὔσας, καὶ οὕτως ὑψηλὰς καὶ μεγάλας, ἃς καὶ δαίμονες ἐνετράπησαν· αἰδοῦ μαι δὲ τὴν ὁμοτιμίαν τοῦ Πνεύματος· φοβοῦμαι δὲ τὴν ὡρισμένην ἀπειλὴν τοῖς εἰς αὐτὸ βλασφημοῦσι. Βλασφημία δὲ, οὐχ ἡ θεολογία, τὸ δὲ ἀλλοτριοῦν τῆς θεότητος. Καὶ τηρητέον ἐνταῦθα, ὅτι τὸ μὲν βλασφημούμενον, ὁ Κύριος ἦν· τὸ δὲ ἐκδικούμενον, τὸ Πνεῦ μα τὸ ἅγιον, δῆλον ὡς Κύριος. Οὐ φέρω ἀφώτιστος εἶναι μετὰ τὸ φώτισμα, παραχαράσσων τι τῶν τριῶν, εἰς ἃ βεβάπτισμαι, καὶ ὄντως ἐνταφῆναι τῷ ὕδατι, οὐκ εἰς ἀναγέννησιν, ἀλλ' εἰς νέκρω σιν τελειούμενος. ΙΒʹ. Τολμῶ τι φθέγξασθαι, ὦ Τριάς· καὶ συγγνώμη τῇ ἀπονοίᾳ· περὶ ψυχῆς γὰρ ὁ κίνδυνος. Εἰκών εἰμι καὶ αὐτὸς Θεοῦ, τῆς ἄνω δόξης, εἰ καὶ κάτω τέθειμαι. Οὐ πείθομαι τῷ ὁμοτίμῳ σώζεσθαι. Εἰ μὴ Θεὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, θεωτήτω πρῶτον, καὶ οὕτω θεούτω με τὸν ὁμότιμον. Νῦν δὲ τίς ἡ ἀπάτη τῆς χάριτος, μᾶλλον δὲ, τῶν διδόντων τὴν χάριν, ὡς εἰς Θεὸν πιστεῦσαι, καὶ ἀνελθεῖν ἄθεον; ἄλλο καθ ομολογῆσαι, καὶ ἄλλο διδάσκεσθαι; οἵαι τῶν λόγων αἱ κλοπαὶ καὶ ἀπάται, δι' ἄλλης ἐρωτήσεως καὶ ὁμολογίας, εἰς ἄλλο φέρουσαι; Οἴμοι τῆς λαμπρότητος, εἰ μετὰ τὸν λουτρὸν μεμελάνωμαι, εἰ λαμπροτέρους ὁρῶ τοὺς οὔπω κεκαθαρμένους, εἰ τῇ τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ κακοδοξίᾳ κυβεύομαι, εἰ ζητῶ Πνεῦμα κρεῖττον, καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκω! Δός μοι λου τρὸν δεύτερον, καὶ περὶ τοῦ πρώτου κακῶς ἐννόησον. Τί μοι φθονεῖς τῆς τελείας ἀναγεννήσεως; τί με ποιεῖς, ναὸν ὄντα τοῦ Πνεύματος ὡς Θεοῦ, κατοικη τήριον κτίσματος; τί τὸ μὲν τιμᾷς τῶν ἐμῶν, τὸ δὲ ἀτιμάζεις κακῶς θεότητι διαιτῶν, ἵν' ἐμοὶ τέ μῃς τὸ χάρισμα, μᾶλλον δὲ, αὐτὸν ἐμὲ τῷ χαρίσματι; Ἢ τὸ πᾶν τίμησον, ὦ καινὲ θεολόγε, ἢ τὸ πᾶν ἀτίμασον, ἵνα, κἂν ἀσεβῇς, ἀλλὰ σεαυτῷ γε ἀκόλουθος ᾖς, μὴ κρίνων ἀνίσως φύσιν ὁμότιμον.
thought_title: The Son and Spirit share all that the Father has
orientation: Gregory continues his doctrinal statement, arguing that the Son and Holy Spirit share the full divinity of the Father.
pass_a_gloss: 10. For about the Father, why is it necessary even to speak, when one must spare him, since all have been preoccupied by natural conceptions, which fact is conceded by all. Even if he bore the first things of dishonor, having been first divided with respect to Good and Creator by the ancient innovation. But about the Son and the Holy Spirit, consider how simply and briefly we may discuss. If anyone has anything of these to say as changeable or alterable, or measured by time or by place or by power or by activity, or not good by nature, or not moved by itself, or not deciding by itself, or a servant, or a hymn singer, or one fearing, or one being set free, or not numbered together, let him show this, and we will accept it, being glorified with the dignity of fellow servants, even if we suffer loss in regard to God. But if all things whatever the Father has belong to the Son, except causation, and all things whatever belong to the Son belong also to the Spirit, except sonship, and except whatever things are said about him in bodily manner on account of my human being and my salvation, in order that having taken what is mine he may grant what is his own through the new mingling, stop raving at last, O sophists of empty words, with fallings down right there. And why do you die, house of Israel, that I may lament you from Scripture. 11. As for me, I revere the titles of the Word, being so many and so high and great, which even demons revered. And I revere the equal honor of the Spirit. And I fear the appointed threat against those who blaspheme against it. Blasphemy is not the true doctrine about God, but the excluding from divinity. And it must be observed here, that what was blasphemed was the Lord, but what avenged was the Holy Spirit, clearly as Lord. I cannot bear to be without light after the enlightenment, falsifying any of the three into whom I was baptized, and to have been truly buried with the water, being completed not into new birth but into death. 12. I dare to utter something, O Trinity, and pardon for the madness, for the danger concerns soul. I myself am also image of God, of the glory above, even if I have been placed below. I am not persuaded to be saved by one of equal honor. If the Holy Spirit is not God, let it first make God, and thus make me God, me the one of equal honor. But now what is the deceit of grace, or rather of those giving grace, so as to believe toward God and to come up without God. Is it one thing to confess and another thing to be taught. What thefts and deceits of words are these, bearing through another question and confession toward another thing. Woe for the brightness, if after the baptism I have been blackened, if I see brighter those not yet cleansed, if I am gambled by the wrong opinion of the baptizer, if I seek a stronger Spirit and do not find. Give me a second baptism, and think badly about the first. Why do you begrudge me the complete new birth. Why do you make me, being temple of the Spirit as God, a dwelling place of creation. Why do you honor one part of my things and dishonor the other, conducting yourself badly toward divinity, in order that you may cut the gift for me, or rather me myself with the gift. Either honor the whole, O new theologian, or dishonor the whole, so that even if you are impious, yet you may be consistent with yourself, not judging unequally a nature of equal honor.

lemmas.gloss: causation, being cause, here the Father being uncaused cause
mingling, intermingling of divine and human

choices.why: means the Father as cause, not general cause
the distinctive property of the Son reserved from the Spirit
alienating from, not making other; uses glossary divinity
dative with living verb means conduct toward, not dividing

bible_refs.note: Καὶ ἵνα τί ἀποθνήσκετε, οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ

pass_b_english: What need is there even to speak about the Father, whom all agree to spare, since they are already possessed by their natural notions of him? He did bear the first dishonor, for he was the first whom the old innovation divided into the Good and the Creator. But about the Son and the Holy Spirit, consider how simply and briefly we will argue. If anyone can show that either of them is changeable or alterable, or measured by time or place or power or activity, or not good by nature, or not self-moving, or not free, or a servant, or a singer of hymns, or afraid, or set free, or not counted together with God, let him prove it, and we will accept it. Then we will be glorified with the dignity of fellow servants, even if we lose God by it.

But if all that the Father has belongs to the Son except causation, and all that belongs to the Son belongs also to the Spirit except sonship and whatever is said of the Son in bodily terms for the sake of my humanity and my salvation, since he took what is mine in order to grant what is his through the new mingling, then stop your raving at last, you sophists of empty words, whose phrases fall flat on the spot. "Why will you die, O house of Israel?" (Ezekiel 33:11)—am I to lament you from Scripture?

For my part, I revere the titles of the Word. They are so many, so high and great, that even demons stood in awe of them. I revere the equal honor of the Spirit. I fear the appointed threat against those who blaspheme against him. And blasphemy is not true teaching about God. It is the excluding of the Spirit from divinity. Mark this well: the one blasphemed was the Lord, and the one avenged was the Holy Spirit, clearly as Lord. I cannot bear to be unenlightened after enlightenment, falsifying any of the three into whom I was baptized, and so to be truly buried in the water only to be finished not for new birth but for death.

I dare to utter something, O Trinity, and forgive my recklessness, for the danger concerns the soul. I myself am an image of God, of the glory above, even though I have been set below. I am not convinced to be saved by one of equal honor with myself. If the Holy Spirit is not God, let him first be made God, and then let him make me God, his equal in honor. As it is, what is this trick of grace, or rather of those who give the grace, that I should believe in God and come up without God? That I should confess one thing and be taught another? What thefts and cheats of argument are these, which carry me by one question and confession to something else?

Woe for that brightness, if I am darkened after baptism, if I see those not yet cleansed brighter than I am, if I am gambled away by the false teaching of the one who baptizes me, if I seek a greater Spirit and cannot find him! Give me a second baptism, and think ill of the first. Why do you begrudge me a perfect new birth? Why do you make me, who am a temple of the Spirit as God, into a dwelling place of creation? Why do you honor one part of me and dishonor the other, conducting yourself badly toward divinity, so as to cut the gift away from me, or rather to cut me myself off together with the gift? Either honor the whole, you new theologian, or dishonor the whole, so that even if you are impious you are at least consistent with yourself, and do not judge unequally a nature of equal honor.
notes: αὐτοῦ πιπτόντων shows number mismatch singular genitive with plural participle; possibly adverbial αὐτοῦ meaning right there, or corrupt for αὐτῶν; glossed neutrally as fallings down right there
εἰ καὶ Θεὸν ζημιούμεθα is ambiguous between suffering loss of God and being punished in regard to God; glossed neutrally
θεωτήτω and θεούτω forms uncertain in voice; glossed as active make God with implied object
spacing breaks in Πνεύ ματος, ῥη μάτων, λου τρὸν, νέκρω σιν, κατοικη τήριον read as single words

problems.quote: even if God punishes us for it
problems.why: The Greek says we would be deprived of, or lose, God. It does not say God punishes us. The sense is changed.
problems.fix: even if we lose God by it.

problems.quote: together with whatever is said of the Son in bodily terms
problems.source_quote: πλὴν τῆς υἱότητος, καὶ τῶν ὅσα σωματικῶς περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγεται
problems.why: The bodily statements are a second exception, introduced by πλὴν. 'Together with' makes them something the Spirit shares, which reverses the claim.
problems.fix: except sonship and whatever is said of the Son in bodily terms for the sake of my humanity

problems.quote: the one who avenged was the Holy Spirit
problems.source_quote: τὸ δὲ ἐκδικούμενον, τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
problems.why: ἐκδικούμενον is passive and parallel to “blasphemed”: the Spirit is the one avenged, not the avenger.
problems.fix: the one avenged was the Holy Spirit, clearly as Lord
problems.ruling: ἐκδικούμενον is passive and parallels βλασφημούμενον. The Spirit is the one avenged, not the avenger, so the English reverses the agency.

problems.quote: And let Gregory lament over you with Scripture
problems.source_quote: ἵν' ἐκ τῆς Γραφῆς ὑμᾶς ὀδύρωμαι
problems.why: Gregory himself utters the lament in the first person so that he may bewail them from Scripture.
problems.fix: “Why will you die, O house of Israel?”—so that I may lament you from the Scripture.
problems.ruling: ὀδύρωμαι is first person, so the speaker laments. 'Let Gregory lament' turns the speaker into a third person the source never names.

problems.quote: consider, Gregory says, how simply and briefly we will argue.
problems.source_quote: σκοπεῖτε ὡς ἁπλῶς καὶ συντόμως διαλεξώμεθα
problems.why: There is no narrator. Gregory himself tells the hearers to consider the argument.
problems.fix: consider how simply and briefly we will argue.
problems.ruling: διαλεξώμεθα and σκοπεῖτε are the speaker's own address. 'Gregory says' is an interpolation that makes the voice reported.

problems.quote: For my part, Gregory says, I revere the titles of the Word.
problems.source_quote: Ὡς ἔγωγε αἰδοῦμαι μὲν τὰς τοῦ Λόγου προσηγορίας
problems.why: “Gregory says” turns the speaker’s own first person into reported speech.
problems.fix: For my part, I revere the titles of the Word.
problems.ruling: Ὡς ἔγωγε αἰδοῦμαι is direct first person. 'Gregory says' is added, creating reported speech.

fixed: punishes -> lose God: Greek εἰ καὶ Θεὸν ζημιούμεθα means deprived of God, not punished by God.
together with -> except: Greek πλὴν τῆς υἱότητος, καὶ τῶν ὅσα covers bodily statements as second exception.
who avenged -> avenged: Greek τὸ δὲ ἐκδικούμενον parallels τὸ βλασφημούμενον, passive, the Spirit avenged.
let Gregory lament -> so that I may lament: Greek ἵν᾽ ὀδύρωμαι is Gregory's own first-person lament.
removed 'Gregory says,': Greek σκοπεῖτε...διαλεξώμεθα is Gregory's direct address, no narrator.
removed 'Gregory says,': Greek Ὡς ἔγωγε αἰδοῦμαι is Gregory's own first person, not reported speech.

problems.quote: We should spare him in reverence, since all people are already possessed by their natural ideas of him.
problems.source_quote: οὗ καὶ τὸ παρὰ πάντων συγκεχωρηκὸς φείδεσθαι ταῖς φυσικαῖς ἐννοίαις προκατειλημμένων
problems.why: Sparing the Father is already everyone's concession; English makes it Gregory's exhortation and adds reverence.
problems.fix: What need is there even to speak of the Father, whom all agree to spare, already held by their natural notions?
problems.ruling: Source: sparing the Father is a concession 'παρὰ πάντων συγκεχωρηκὸς' of all; English turns it into Gregory's exhortation 'We should spare him in reverence', adding reverence and changing agency.

problems.quote: so that I may lament you from Scripture
problems.source_quote: ἵν' ἐκ τῆς Γραφῆς ὑμᾶς ὀδύρωμαι;
problems.why: The Greek is a rhetorical question; English states an unfinished purpose.
problems.fix: "Why will you die, O house of Israel?" (Ezekiel 33:11)—am I to lament you from Scripture?
problems.ruling: Source 'Καὶ ἵνα τί ἀποθνήσκετε… ἵν' ἐκ τῆς Γραφῆς ὑμᾶς ὀδύρωμαι;' is a question; English drops it, leaving a dangling purpose clause with the question misrendered.

fixed: [agency] fixed: removed exhortation/reverence; sparing is the concession of all (τὸ παρὰ πάντων συγκεχωρηκὸς φείδεσθαι) held by natural notions (ταῖς φυσικαῖς ἐννοίαις προκατειλημμένων).
[modality] fixed: changed purpose clause to rhetorical question for ἵν᾽ ... ὀδύρωμαι; —am I to lament you from Scripture?

last_rejected.quote: Then we will be glorified with the dignity of fellow servants, even if we lose God by it.
last_rejected.source_quote: συνδούλων σεμνότητι δοξαζόμενοι, εἰ καὶ Θεὸν ζημιούμεθα
last_rejected.why: Source is a participle: 'we will accept it, being honored by the dignity of fellow servants'; English makes a separate future sentence, 'Then', and shifts the logic slightly. Minor reshaping, but 'Then' is added.
last_rejected.fix: we will welcome it, glorified by the dignity of fellow servants, even if we lose God by it.
last_rejected.ruling: δοξαζόμενοι is attendant to στέρξομεν; 'Then' only splits the clause. σεμνότητι and Θεὸν ζημιούμεθα still mean honor and loss of God.

last_rejected.quote: whose phrases fall flat on the spot
last_rejected.why: Genitive absolute 'αὐτοῦ πιπτόντων' means 'as they themselves (your words) fall' or 'while he/it falls'; 'on the spot' is an invented sense, and 'fall flat' is loose.
last_rejected.fix: since your words fall of themselves.
last_rejected.ruling: Adverb αὐτοῦ means 'on the spot' and cannot agree with plural πιπτόντων; 'fall flat' renders ῥημάτων falling/failing.
